newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Buyers boost medium to long Belgian linear Bonds.
newsitem.headline: Buyers boost medium to long Belgian linear Bonds.

text.p: A burst of foreign and domestic buying boosted medium- to long-maturity Belgian linear bonds on Thursday as a bullish mood and technical oversold signals rampaged over more cautious voices, traders said.
"It was in two phases," one trader said. "This morning it was all along the curve except for the very short end. This afternoon it was at the middle to long end but more selectively," he added.
The benchmark 2006 OLO was a strong performer, as were the 2008 and 2012 maturities. The 2015 maturity bond, by contrast, found sellers coming out of the woodwork.
"OLO 16 (2008) was the star of the day. It outperformed the market," one trader said.
Traders said foreign buyers originally focused on the benchmark OLO 9 and then spread their attention to neighbouring maturities, pushing the market to easily outperform Bunds.
But not all traders were convinced that the rally was sustainable.

"The (U.S.) PPI figures today could easily show through in higher CPI figures tomorrow, and if that is the case this market will go rapidly into reverse," one trader said. "Fundamentally there is no reason for this strength."
The producer price index figure, which had been expected up 0.1 percent month-on-month, actually came in at plus 0.3 percent.
The consumer price index, due at 1230 GMT on Friday, is seen flat month-on-month and up 1.3 percent year-on-year.
Traders said the dollar could also have an impact, predicting a flattening of the yield curve if the currency remained at current levels for much longer.
